subject.title: [Bug]: Subagent completion silently lost — no retry, no notification, no auto-restart on timeout

question: Should OpenClaw make subagent completion delivery a durable at-least-once contract, or keep best-effort announce with clearer bounded failure visibility?
rationale: The remaining behavior spans retry timing, duplicate-send prevention, task-ledger truth, requester wakeup semantics, restart/orphan preservation, and user-visible failure policy, so code inspection cannot safely choose the permanent delivery contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design Durable Completion Delivery
options.body: Make completion payloads durable with explicit pending, delivered, failed, recoverable, and discarded states plus idempotent channel delivery before closing this issue.

options.title: Ship Bounded Visibility First
options.body: Accept a narrower retry/failure-notification mitigation now while keeping the durable spool and active-run race issues open as follow-up work.

options.title: Keep Best-Effort Announce
options.body: Document best-effort announce as the intended contract and close only if maintainers decide durable completion delivery is out of scope.

recommendation.title: Design Durable Completion Delivery
recommendation.body: Make completion payloads durable with explicit pending, delivered, failed, recoverable, and discarded states plus idempotent channel delivery before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has the strongest recent history signal on the current subagent delivery-state and task-status paths, plus related partial-fix commentary.
